lines.3: 「Pay it no mind! A man does not concern himself with trifles! Gahahaha!」
lines.4: 「I'm not a man. I'm a modern lady.」
lines.6: 「He is easily influenced. Wonder what got into him this time.」
lines.10: 「No, no. Younger students should greet people energetically.」
lines.11: Yashi skewered him with a look reserved for filth.
lines.12: Fukahire ignored it and slapped her on the back.
lines.13: 「So overbearing... What is wrong with him?」
lines.19: 「Everyone, the retreat is now over! Well done.」
lines.21: 「Director! Please continue teaching me about manliness!」
lines.22: So Heizo was the strange influence.
lines.28: 「Yoppi, could you help me organize some documents?」
lines.29: 「Sorry. I told you I have plans today...」
lines.33: In the end, only the Princess and I remained in the council room.
lines.35: 「There. We have finished covering everything the sluggish athletics committee left behind.」
lines.36: 「Bad luck, the committee chair catching a cold.」
lines.37: 「Indeed. Managing one's health is part of the job.」
lines.41: 「It does. A privilege of the student council president, perhaps.」
lines.42: 「Sometimes I skip class and stare at the sea from here. It is rather relaxing.」
lines.43: 「You can skip and still stay first. This school is honestly beneath your level.」
lines.44: 「Why did you choose Ryuumeikan? Because it's close?」
lines.46: 「And its many events promised I would not be bored.」
lines.49: 「Some people reach the summit they desired, only to be crushed by loneliness and distrust.」
lines.50: 「Part of me thinks they were weak and never fit to rule. Another part knows it could happen to me.」
lines.54: 「How dense. They say this place is full of remarkable people, so I came looking for companions I could speak honestly with.」
lines.55: 「And I was exactly right. I met Yoppi and discovered Otome-senpai.」
lines.56: 「I have invited them to work at Kiriya as my aides someday. Otome-senpai would be my bodyguard.」
lines.59: 「My goal is on a grand scale.」
lines.60: 「Wouldn't the best school give you promising people and connections in every field?」
lines.61: 「Parties provide enough connections. I want reliable companions.」
lines.62: 「I want to see how far I can go.」
lines.63: The Princess reached toward the setting sun and clenched her fist.
lines.64: 「Few people your age say things like that.」
lines.67: 「I haven't chosen one profession I absolutely want.」
lines.68: 「A healthy, happy life might be enough for me.」
lines.70: 「No. That view is important. Essential, even.」
lines.71: 「My goal is to keep ordinary people like you alive, barely, and extract their money. A pyramid needs a solid base.」
lines.74: 「Your ambition is admirable, but I worry.」
lines.76: 「You're an idiot in odd ways, Princess.」
lines.78: 「How irritating. 'Idiot,' says a man whose name never appears on the academic honor board.」
lines.79: 「Being good at school and being an idiot are different things.」
lines.81: 「You spoke seriously about your dream, so I'm answering seriously.」
lines.83: 「However grand you act, I don't think you can truly use people or become ruthless.」
lines.85: 「...That I cannot ignore. Most people are merely pieces to me.」
lines.87: 「But I don't feel like a piece. I think we're having fun.」
lines.88: 「What are you imagining? You are nothing but a piece.」
lines.90: 「Someone who truly used people as pieces probably wouldn't say so to their faces.」
lines.92: 「Right now, you seem more like someone who admires the idea of using pieces.」
lines.96: The Princess beckoned with one finger.
lines.99: Her face drew close, setting my heart racing.
lines.100: 「Who do you think you are, talking down to me, idiot?!」
lines.103: 「Talking as if you understand everything! That made me angry. Very angry.」
lines.104: 「If I say you're a piece, then someone like you is a piece!」
lines.105: Th-the Princess was getting all worked up.
lines.106: 「I only want to use you for various things.」
lines.108: 「Fine! If you insist, I will show you. I had doubts about this, but you helped me make up my mind.」
